title: Geo-SMILE: Statistical Model-Agnostic Interpretability with Local Explanations for Geospatial Machine Learning
abstract: arXiv:2611.31731v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Conventional post-hoc explanation methods were developed largely for non-spatial inputs and often provide limited explicit treatment of geographic context. We introduce Geo-SMILE, a model-agnostic framework that distinguishes substantive Feature explanation from geographic-position response through complementary perturbation branches. The Feature branch masks substantive predictors while retaining observed coordinates; the Geo branch relocates geographic units while holding substantive predictors fixed. Following the statistical-distance-weighted surrogate principle of SMILE, input-distribution Wasserstein distances determine coalition locality weights and weighted Ridge surrogates approximate expected black-box predictions. GeoSensitivity, signed in the keep orientation, quantifies fitted-model responses to geographic-player relocation under the specified design. translated_title: Geo-SMILE：面向地理空间机器学习的统计模型无关可解释性与局部解释方法
translated_abstract: 传统的后置（post-hoc）解释方法主要是为非空间输入开发的，通常对地理背景缺乏明确的处理。我们提出Geo-SMILE，一个模型无关的框架，通过互补的扰动分支将实质性特征解释与地理位置响应区分开来。特征分支在保留观测坐标的同时屏蔽实质性预测变量；地理分支则在固定实质性预测变量的同时重新定位地理单元。遵循SMILE的统计距离加权替代模型原则，输入分布的Wasserstein距离决定联盟的局部性权重，加权Ridge替代模型用于近似期望的黑箱预测。GeoSensitivity以保留方向为符号，量化在指定设计下拟合模型对地理单元重新定位的响应。在赫尔市的犯罪预测、西雅图的房价预测等任务上（摘要原文在此处截断）……
tldr: 提出Geo-SMILE框架，通过互补的特征屏蔽与地理重定位两个扰动分支以及距离加权的替代模型，将实质性特征解释与地理空间位置响应区分开来，为地理空间机器学习提供模型无关的局部可解释性。
en_tdlr: Geo-SMILE is a model-agnostic framework that separates substantive feature explanations from geographic-position responses through complementary perturbation branches and distance-weighted surrogate models, enabling local interpretability for geospatial machine learning.
